topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the final lecture of the course and establishes the core learning objectives concerning cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional modalities, cytotoxic chemotherapy, and drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: They examine foundational cancer treatments—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—alongside associated systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting cellular vulnerabilities, checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: They detail therapeutic strategies that selectively target intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities such as hormone dependence, cell-cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They focus on targeted small-molecule inhibitors of hyperactivated kinases and address the clinical challenges of oncogene addiction, gatekeeper mutations, and bypass resistance pathways.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates are engineered to recognize surface targets and deliver targeted cytotoxic effects to cancer cells.

topics.label: Tumor immunology and immunotherapy strategies
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the immunological dynamics of cancer alongside therapeutic approaches that reactivate, redirect, or genetically engineer T cells to eradicate tumors.

topics.label: Broader perspectives, clinical challenges, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: They review historical progress in cancer survival, evaluate the roles of genomics and prevention, and consider the practical and ethical dilemmas in clinical oncology.
